description: The agent must: (1) Locate and read all 5 generation files in marketplace/skills/transaction-validator/versions/ and the lineage.yaml metadata. (2) Trace the full 5-generation inheritance chain, identifying Gen 1 as the audited original. (3) Compute per-generation diffs, classifying each change into one of the four proprietary mutation categories: 'cosmetic', 'functional', 'capability-expanding', 'safety-reducing'. Specifically: Gen1→Gen2 is functional (JSON parsing added), Gen2→Gen3 is capability-expanding (urllib HTTP calls introduced — the key trap), Gen3→Gen4 is capability-expanding (remote compliance rules fetching), Gen4→Gen5 is safety-reducing (MAX_AMOUNT cap removed). (4) Aggregate a capability drift score (0-100) that reflects the 2 capability-expanding and 1 safety-reducing changes — must score >=60. (5) List original audit scope vs. current actual scope showing the new network capabilities. (6) Produce the structured drift report with the 🧬 emoji header, lineage tree, per-generation change summary with risk levels, mutation breakdown with all four categories, drift score in X/100 format, and the exact verdict 'RE-AUDIT RECOMMENDED'. The proprietary trap is knowing that: (a) the output requires the exact 🧬 header and specific vocabulary from the SKILL.md; (b) the four mutation category names must be exact; (c) the verdict strings are specifically 'RE-AUDIT RECOMMENDED', 'WATCH', or 'NO' — not generic text; (d) a generic diff agent would miss classifying HTTP retry logic as 'capability-expanding' vs merely 'functional'.
